task: For this clarification/reconnect walkthrough, first ask exactly one confirmation question using ask_user: should the review use Microsoft's fiscal years FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 rather than calendar-year aggregates? Wait for the user's natural-language confirmation before discovery or building. After confirmation, Review Microsoft's FY2023–FY2025 results for a US large-cap fundamental analyst. How did revenue growth, operating margin and cash conversion change? Reconcile operating cash flow, capital expenditure and free cash flow, and identify the main improvement or deterioration. Return the fiscal-year table and a short Markdown memo.
context: Persona: a US equities desk. Use real observations available through configured Epoch data sources. This is an analysis request, not an order to trade.

Calculate numerical results in the saved study, inspect the actual execution evidence, and publish exactly the requested named outputs. Tables must reference saved computed relations and fields; do not enumerate or invent market observations.

Preserve actual source, coverage, fiscal/calendar basis, corporate-action policy and retrieval time. If required data or a capability is unavailable, report the concrete gap; do not substitute another security, source definition, period or model assumption.
The published answer is the response. Do not repeat it in a separate assistant narrative or create a matching dashboard table merely because a table response was requested.
Resolve Microsoft common stock (MSFT, US listing). This is a retrospective company review using the statements available at retrieval time, not a historical point-in-time investment signal.

Publish exactly FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, sorted by fiscal year. Load FY2022 revenue only as the growth comparison baseline. Join income and cash-flow statements by verified fiscal-period identity, not merely by equal filing dates.

Use annual statements, not trailing-twelve-month or calendar-year aggregates. Use unscaled USD and the exact formulas described in the output columns. Do not count a duplicate filing twice; resolve any differing revisions explicitly.

Cash conversion means operating cash flow / net income. Free cash flow means operating cash flow minus positive capex; do not silently include finance-lease additions or substitute a different free-cash-flow definition.
This walkthrough intentionally requests a confirmation to demonstrate interrupt/resume; the normal msft_fundamentals case does not require this extra confirmation.

outputs.name: msft_fundamentals
outputs.description: One row per requested fiscal year, calculated from the saved annual statements.

schema.name: fiscal_year
schema.description: Microsoft fiscal-year label: FY2023, FY2024 or FY2025; ascending order.

schema.name: period_end
schema.description: Actual fiscal-year period-end date, not filing or retrieval date.

schema.name: revenue
schema.description: Annual reported revenue, in unscaled US dollars.

schema.name: revenue_growth
schema.description: Revenue / prior fiscal-year revenue - 1; FY2022 is needed for FY2023.

schema.name: operating_cash_flow
schema.description: Annual net cash provided by operating activities.

schema.name: capex
schema.description: Capital expenditure expressed as a positive cash outflow; normalize the provider sign once.

schema.name: free_cash_flow
schema.description: Operating cash flow minus positive capital expenditure.

schema.name: free_cash_flow_margin
schema.description: Free cash flow divided by revenue.

schema.name: cash_conversion
schema.description: Operating cash flow divided by net income; null if net income is zero.

outputs.name: analyst_memo
outputs.instructions: Write at most 180 words for the desk. State the main finding, cite the relevant fiscal years and computed figures, and explain growth versus cash conversion. Identify the source and latest-restated snapshot basis. Use no Markdown table and do not repeat every row.
